active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.minimize with SLSQP for direct circle position optimization
active_paradigms.description: Optimize all 52 circle coordinates (x,y for each of 26 circles) directly using scipy.optimize.minimize with SLSQP method. Define objective as negative sum of radii (to minimize). Add explicit constraints: (1) each circle stays within unit square: x-r >= 0, x+r <= 1, y-r >= 0, y+r <= 1 where r is computed as min distance to walls and other circles; (2) non-overlap: distance between circles >= sum of radii. Use multiple random starting points to escape local minima. This removes the rigid row structure entirely and lets circles find arbitrary optimal positions.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Maximize sum of radii by finding optimal positions for all circles simultaneously
active_paradigms.cautions: SLSQP may struggle with many constraints (52 variables + ~350 overlap constraints). Use proper constraint formulation, reasonable bounds [0,1] for positions, and multiple starting points. May need to reformulate as penalty-based objective if constraint handling is too slow.

active_paradigms.idea: Use greedy corner-first placement with largest-minimum-distance heuristic
active_paradigms.description: Implement a deterministic constructive algorithm that places circles in order of priority: first place 4 circles in corners (optimizing their radii), then place remaining 22 circles one at a time. For each new circle, scan a fine grid of candidate positions and select the position that maximizes the minimum distance to all existing circles and square boundaries. This greedy approach exploits the fact that corner circles can be larger and provides a fast, deterministic packing without any optimization calls. The grid resolution and placement order can be tuned for better results.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Maximize sum of radii through intelligent placement order and position selection
active_paradigms.cautions: Greedy algorithms can get stuck in local optima. May need to try different corner circle sizes or placement orders. Grid resolution affects both speed and quality - too coarse misses good positions, too fine is slow.

active_paradigms.idea: Use mixed corner-center pattern with parameterized optimization
active_paradigms.description: Place 4 circles explicitly in corners with parameterized radii, then pack remaining 22 circles in a hexagonal pattern in the center region. Optimize 4 corner radii + 2 center pattern parameters (spacing and offset) using scipy.optimize.minimize with Nelder-Mead. This hybrid approach explicitly handles edge effects (corners get special treatment) while maintaining efficient packing in the center. The corner circles can have larger radii than center circles, which may be optimal for square container packing. Test different corner configurations (equal radii vs asymmetric).
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Maximize sum of radii by exploiting corner space while maintaining dense center packing
active_paradigms.cautions: Corner circles must not overlap with center pattern circles - need careful constraint checking. The transition between corner and center regions must be smooth to avoid wasted space. May need to adjust corner placement positions (not just at exact corners) for better results.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution for global optimization of circle positions and radii
tried_paradigms.description: Implement a penalty-based objective function that minimizes negative sum of radii plus large penalties for constraint violations (overlaps and out-of-bounds). Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution to search the 78-dimensional space (26 centers × 2 coordinates + 26 radii). The DE method is ideal for this non-convex problem as it can escape local minima. Set bounds: centers in [0,1]×[0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Use penalty coefficients that scale with violation severity. Run with multiple workers and high maxiter for thorough search. This replaces the fixed grid with a global search that can discover irregular optimal patterns.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii while maintaining validity through penalty-based constraints
tried_paradigms.cautions: Constraint penalties must be large enough to enforce validity but not overwhelm the objective. Use seed for reproducibility. Monitor convergence and may need 1000+ function evaluations.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.spatial.Voronoi to construct non-overlapping packing from optimized centers
tried_paradigms.description: Create a two-stage constructor: first optimize 26 circle centers using scipy.optimize.minimize with SLSQP, then compute radii from Voronoi cell boundaries to guarantee non-overlap. For each center, compute its Voronoi cell using scipy.spatial.Voronoi, then set radius to minimum distance from center to any cell edge or square boundary. This automatically satisfies non-overlap constraints by construction. The optimization only needs to handle center positions and boundary constraints, reducing the constraint complexity significantly. This exploits geometric structure rather than explicit overlap constraints.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: center positions to maximize Voronoi-derived radii sum
tried_paradigms.cautions: Voronoi diagram can be unstable for edge cases; use scipy.spatial.Voronoi with proper handling. Need to handle points on convex hull carefully. Boundary constraints still apply.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.linprog for linearized packing with hexagonal layer construction
tried_paradigms.description: Design a structured hexagonal layer packing: place circles in staggered rows with hexagonal spacing (optimal for infinite packing). Use scipy.optimize.linprog to solve for optimal layer spacing and offsets that maximize total radii while respecting square boundaries. Linearize the problem by assuming fixed hexagonal pattern with variable parameters (row spacing, column spacing, offsets). The linear program optimizes these geometric parameters subject to boundary constraints. This exploits the known optimal structure of dense circle packings while accounting for square container edge effects through the linear optimization.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: hexagonal pattern parameters (spacing, offsets) to maximize sum of radii
tried_paradigms.cautions: Hexagonal pattern may not be globally optimal for n=26 in square; linearization assumes fixed structure. May need to try multiple layer configurations (e.g., 5-5-5-5-4-2 or similar distributions).

tried_paradigms.idea: Direct nonlinear optimization with scipy.optimize.minimize using SLSQP
tried_paradigms.description: Optimize all 78 variables (52 positions + 26 radii) simultaneously using scipy.optimize.minimize with SLSQP method. Formulate the problem as maximizing sum of radii subject to explicit constraints: boundary constraints (x-r>=0, x+r<=1, y-r>=0, y+r<=1) and non-overlap constraints (distance >= r1+r2 for all pairs). Use a penalty-based objective function that heavily penalizes constraint violations. Start from a good hexagonal initialization to help convergence. This directly optimizes the objective rather than using a heuristic pattern.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii (primary metric) by optimizing all circle positions and radii simultaneously
tried_paradigms.cautions: SLSQP may get stuck in local optima - use multiple random restarts. Constraint formulation must be careful to avoid numerical issues. May need to use penalty functions instead of hard constraints if SLSQP struggles. Set appropriate bounds (0 <= x,y <= 1, 0 <= r).

tried_paradigms.description: Use scipy.spatial.Voronoi to generate an adaptive packing pattern. Start with a good initial point distribution (e.g., hexagonal or random with minimum separation), compute Voronoi tessellation, then place each circle at its Voronoi cell centroid. Size each circle based on the minimum distance from centroid to cell vertices (inscribed circle in Voronoi cell). This naturally creates non-uniform radii that adapt to local space availability, especially near boundaries. Optionally iterate: after placing circles, recompute Voronoi on the actual centers and adjust.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii by exploiting local geometry to maximize space utilization near boundaries
tried_paradigms.cautions: Voronoi cells at boundary are unbounded - need to clip to unit square. Initial point distribution matters greatly. May need to handle degenerate cases. The relationship between Voronoi cell size and circle radius is not trivial - use minimum distance to vertices as radius upper bound.

tried_paradigms.description: Model circles as charged particles with repulsive forces and use scipy.optimize.minimize to find equilibrium. Define an energy function: E = sum over all pairs of (1/distance)^k for overlapping circles plus penalty for boundary violations. The repulsion is stronger when circles are closer (k=2-4). Use minimize with L-BFGS-B to find the configuration that minimizes total energy. This physics-based approach naturally pushes circles apart and toward available space, often finding better packings than rigid patterns. After optimization, scale radii to maximum feasible values.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii by using physics-inspired repulsion to find efficient packing configurations
tried_paradigms.cautions: Energy function must be carefully designed to avoid numerical instability when distances approach zero. May need to add small epsilon to distances. The method finds local minima - use multiple random initializations. After finding positions, need a separate step to maximize radii while respecting constraints.
